intro.title: Debounced Search
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a real-time search input component that filters a list of items as you type, but with a performance optimization. You will learn how to implement a debounced search, which delays the search execution until the user stops typing for a brief moment, preventing excessive updates. The core programming concept involves using a timer to control function calls, combined with React state and event handling. You will work with React hooks like useState and useEffect, along with JavaScript's setTimeout and clearTimeout functions. By the end, you'll have a functional search bar that efficiently handles user input without overwhelming the app with rapid state changes.
intro.usecase: Debounced search is essential for responsive user interfaces that handle real-time input. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce search bars that filter products as you type, dashboard data tables with live filtering, and form autocomplete fields that fetch suggestions. This technique prevents excessive API calls while maintaining immediate feedback, improving both performance and user experience. Developers implement debouncing in search components, filter panels, and any interactive element where user input triggers expensive operations like network requests or complex calculations.
